stem: Gold plated ornaments is the example of ________.
solution: Gold plating on ornaments is done by depositing a thin layer of gold on the article using electric current through an electrolyte. This process of coating one metal over another using electrolysis is called electroplating.

stem: The functioning of the satellite launch vehicle is based on ________.
solution: A satellite launch vehicle works on the principle of rocket propulsion. The burnt fuel gases are ejected backward at high speed and, by Newton's third law of motion, an equal and opposite reaction thrust pushes the vehicle forward (upward).

stem: ________ is one of the combustible components of L.P.G.
solution: L.P.G. (Liquefied Petroleum Gas) mainly contains the combustible hydrocarbons butane and propane. Among the given options, propane is a combustible component of L.P.G.

stem: The power of a convex lens of focal length 25 cm is ________.
solution: Power \(P = \dfrac{1}{f\ (\text{in metre})}\). Here \(f = 25\ \mathrm{cm} = 0.25\ \mathrm{m}\), so \(P = \dfrac{1}{0.25} = +4.0\ \mathrm{D}\). The power of a convex (converging) lens is positive.

stem: ________ colour is deviated the least, in the spectrum of white light obtained with a glass prism.
solution: In the dispersion of white light through a glass prism, the deviation depends on wavelength. Red light has the longest wavelength and hence undergoes the least deviation, while violet has the shortest wavelength and the maximum deviation.

stem: Find the odd one out: INSAT, GSAT, IRS, PSLV.
solution: PSLV is the odd one out. INSAT, GSAT and IRS are artificial satellites (satellite systems), whereas PSLV (Polar Satellite Launch Vehicle) is a satellite launch vehicle used to place satellites into orbit.

subtopic: Groups of the Modern Periodic Table
stem: Complete the correlation: Group 1 : Alkali metals : : ________ : Halogens.
solution: Group 17. In the modern periodic table, Group 1 elements are the alkali metals and Group 17 elements are the halogens.

stem: State True or False: An electric motor converts mechanical energy into electrical energy.
solution: False. An electric motor converts electrical energy into mechanical energy. (A device that converts mechanical energy into electrical energy is an electric generator.)

stem:
Write the IUPAC name for the following structural formula:

\(\mathrm{CH_3\!-\!\underset{\underset{\textstyle OH}{|}}{CH}\!-\!CH_3}\)
solution: The compound is \(\mathrm{CH_3\!-\!CH(OH)\!-\!CH_3}\), a three-carbon chain with an \(-\mathrm{OH}\) group on the second carbon. Its IUPAC name is propan-2-ol (isopropyl alcohol).

stem: Give a scientific reason: Atomic radius goes on increasing down a group.
solution: On going down a group, the number of electron shells (energy levels) increases by one for each successive element. This increases the distance of the outermost electrons from the nucleus, and the inner shells also screen (shield) the outer electrons from the nuclear attraction. Although nuclear charge increases, the effect of the added shell dominates, so the atomic radius goes on increasing down a group.

stem: Give a scientific reason: Simple microscope is used for watch repairs.
solution: A simple microscope is a convex lens of short focal length. When a tiny object is placed within its focus, it produces a virtual, erect and magnified image. The parts of a watch are very small, so a watch repairer uses a simple microscope to see an enlarged image of these parts clearly and repair them accurately.

stem: Give a scientific reason: It is recommended to use airtight container for storing oil for long time.
solution: Oils and fats get slowly oxidised by the oxygen of air, which changes their taste and smell; this is called rancidity. An airtight container prevents contact of the oil with atmospheric oxygen, thereby slowing down oxidation and preventing the oil from becoming rancid, so it can be stored for a long time.

stem: An object takes 5 s to reach the ground from a height of 5 m on a planet. What is the value of 'g' on the planet?
solution:
The object falls from rest, so \(u = 0\), \(s = 5\ \mathrm{m}\), \(t = 5\ \mathrm{s}\). Using \(s = ut + \dfrac{1}{2}gt^2\):
\(5 = 0 + \dfrac{1}{2}\times g \times (5)^2 = \dfrac{25g}{2}\).
So \(g = \dfrac{2\times 5}{25} = 0.4\ \mathrm{m/s^2}\).

stem: Draw a neat labelled diagram of Hope's Apparatus.
solution: Hope's apparatus demonstrates the anomalous expansion of water. It consists of a tall cylindrical metal vessel filled with water, with a central circular trough (ledge) around its middle containing a freezing mixture of ice and common salt. Two thermometers are inserted through the vessel wall - one just above the central trough (upper thermometer) and one just below it (lower thermometer). As water near the middle cools, the lower thermometer first falls to about 4 degrees C (as the densest water sinks); later the upper thermometer falls towards 0 degrees C and ice forms at the top, showing water's maximum density at 4 degrees C. (Label: cylindrical vessel with water, central trough with freezing mixture of ice + salt, upper thermometer, lower thermometer.)

stem: State the Laws of Refraction.
solution:
First law: The incident ray, the refracted ray and the normal to the surface at the point of incidence all lie in the same plane.
Second law (Snell's law): For a given pair of media, the ratio of the sine of the angle of incidence to the sine of the angle of refraction is constant. \(\dfrac{\sin i}{\sin r} = n\ (\text{constant})\), where \(n\) is the refractive index of the second medium with respect to the first.

stem: Name the main ore of aluminium.
solution: The main ore of aluminium is bauxite, \(\mathrm{Al_2O_3\cdot 2H_2O}\) (hydrated aluminium oxide).

stem: What impurities are present in aluminium ore?
solution: Bauxite ore (aluminium ore) mainly contains impurities such as ferric oxide \(\mathrm{(Fe_2O_3)}\) and silica \(\mathrm{(SiO_2)}\), along with small amounts of other oxides.

stem: Observe the given figure of Fleming's Left Hand Rule (the thumb shows 'Force of the conductor') and write the labels of 'A' and 'B'.
solution: According to Fleming's Left Hand Rule, when the thumb, forefinger and middle finger of the left hand are held mutually perpendicular: the thumb points in the direction of force (motion) on the conductor, the forefinger in the direction of the magnetic field, and the middle finger in the direction of the current. Since the thumb is labelled 'Force of the conductor', A (forefinger) = direction of Magnetic field and B (middle finger) = direction of Electric current.
figureNote: Figure of a left hand showing Fleming's Left Hand Rule; the thumb is labelled 'Force of the conductor' and two fingers point to blank boxes A and B to be identified (page 2).

stem: Write the demerits of Mendeleev's periodic table.
solution:
Demerits of Mendeleev's periodic table:
- The position of hydrogen could not be fixed (it resembles both alkali metals of Group I and halogens of Group VII).
- Isotopes of an element were not given separate places, though they have different atomic masses.
- The increase in atomic mass from one element to the next is not regular, so the number of elements yet to be discovered could not be predicted.
- In some pairs, an element of higher atomic mass was placed before one of lower atomic mass (anomalous pairs, e.g. Argon before Potassium, Cobalt before Nickel).

stem: State the laws related to the given diagram (a planet moving in an elliptical orbit around the Sun, sweeping equal-area sectors 1, 2 and 3).
solution:
The diagram illustrates Kepler's laws of planetary motion:
- Kepler's First Law (Law of orbits): A planet moves around the Sun in an elliptical orbit with the Sun situated at one of the foci of the ellipse.
- Kepler's Second Law (Law of areas): The line joining a planet and the Sun sweeps out equal areas in equal intervals of time (the shaded sectors 1, 2, 3 have equal areas), so the areal velocity of the planet is constant.
- Kepler's Third Law (Law of periods): The square of the orbital period of a planet is directly proportional to the cube of the mean distance of the planet from the Sun, \(T^2 \propto r^3\).
figureNote: Diagram of an elliptical orbit with the Sun (S) at a focus, a planet at A, and three shaded sectors labelled 1, 2, 3 of equal area swept by the Sun-planet line (page 2).

context: Identify the type of chemical reaction given below:
stem: \(\mathrm{CuSO_4 + Fe \rightarrow FeSO_4 + Cu}\)
solution: This is a displacement reaction. The more reactive metal iron (Fe) displaces the less reactive copper (Cu) from copper sulphate solution.

context: Identify the type of chemical reaction given below:
stem: \(\mathrm{2Mg + O_2 \rightarrow 2MgO}\)
solution: This is a combination reaction (two reactants combine to form a single product). It is also an oxidation reaction, as magnesium is oxidised to magnesium oxide.

context: Identify the type of chemical reaction given below:
stem: \(\mathrm{2KClO_3 \rightarrow 2KCl + 3O_2 \uparrow}\)
solution: This is a decomposition reaction. A single compound, potassium chlorate, breaks down (on heating) into two simpler substances, potassium chloride and oxygen gas.

stem: If the speed of light in a medium is \(1.5 \times 10^{8}\ \mathrm{m/s}\), what is the absolute refractive index of the medium? (Speed of light in vacuum \(= 3 \times 10^{8}\ \mathrm{m/s}\).)
solution: Absolute refractive index \(n = \dfrac{c}{v} = \dfrac{3 \times 10^{8}}{1.5 \times 10^{8}} = 2\). The absolute refractive index of the medium is 2.

context: Read the following paragraph and answer the questions based on it: If heat is exchanged between a hot and cold object, the temperature of the cold object goes on increasing due to gain of energy and the temperature of the hot object goes on decreasing due to loss of energy. The change in temperature continues till the temperatures of both the objects attain the same value. In this process, the cold object gains heat energy and the hot object loses heat energy. If the system of both the objects is isolated from the environment by keeping it inside a heat resistant box, then no energy can flow from inside the box or come into the box.
stem: Heat is transferred from where to where?
solution: Heat is transferred from the hot object (at higher temperature) to the cold object (at lower temperature), until both attain the same temperature.

stem: Which principle do we learn about from this process?
solution: We learn about the principle of heat exchange (also called the principle of calorimetry).

context: Read the following paragraph and answer the questions based on it: If heat is exchanged between a hot and cold object, the temperature of the cold object goes on increasing due to gain of energy and the temperature of the hot object goes on decreasing due to loss of energy. The change in temperature continues till the temperatures of both the objects attain the same value. In this process, the cold object gains heat energy and the hot object loses heat energy. If the system of both the objects is isolated from the environment by keeping it inside a heat resistant box, then no energy can flow from inside the box or come into the box.
stem: How will you state the principle briefly?
solution: Principle of heat exchange: When a hot object and a cold object are kept in contact in an isolated system, the heat energy lost by the hot object is equal to the heat energy gained by the cold object, i.e. heat energy lost = heat energy gained.

stem: Metallurgy
solution: Metallurgy is the science and technology dealing with the extraction of metals from their ores and the refining of these metals for use, including the various processes involved.

stem: Ores
solution: Ores are those minerals from which a metal can be extracted economically and conveniently (i.e. profitably). For example, bauxite is an ore of aluminium.

stem: Gangue.
solution: Gangue is the unwanted impurity such as soil, sand and rocky material present in an ore along with the metal compound. It has to be removed during the concentration (enrichment) of the ore.

stem: State the importance of Space Mission.
solution:
Importance of space missions:
- Communication satellites help in telecommunication, television broadcasting, telephone and internet services.
- Weather satellites help in weather forecasting and giving early warning of cyclones and natural disasters.
- Remote sensing satellites help in surveying natural resources, agriculture, forestry, water resources and land use.
- They help in navigation (GPS), defence, and national security.
- Space missions provide scientific knowledge about the Earth, other planets, the Sun and the universe, aiding research and exploration.

context: Observe the following diagram (a rectangular current-carrying coil ABCD placed between the poles N and S of a magnet, with conducting rings, carbon brushes, axle and a battery) and answer the questions given below:
stem: Write the principle on which the above appliance works.
solution: Principle: When a current-carrying conductor (coil) is placed in a magnetic field, it experiences a mechanical force. The two opposite sides of the coil experience equal and opposite forces (given by Fleming's Left Hand Rule) which form a couple/torque, causing the coil to rotate.
figureNote: Labelled diagram of a DC electric motor: rectangular coil ABCD between N and S poles (magnetic field), split conducting rings R1/R2, carbon brushes B1/B2, axle and battery in the circuit (page 3).

context: Observe the following diagram (a rectangular current-carrying coil ABCD placed between the poles N and S of a magnet, with conducting rings, carbon brushes, axle and a battery) and answer the questions given below:
stem: Write the working of the above appliance.
solution: Working: When current is passed through the coil ABCD placed in the magnetic field, the current flows in opposite directions in sides AB and CD. By Fleming's Left Hand Rule, side AB experiences a force in one direction and side CD experiences an equal force in the opposite direction. This pair of forces forms a couple that rotates the coil. When the coil becomes vertical, the split rings (commutator) change contact with the carbon brushes, reversing the direction of current in the coil. This keeps the force on each side acting in the same rotational sense, so the coil goes on rotating continuously in the same direction.
figureNote: Labelled diagram of a DC electric motor: rectangular coil ABCD between N and S poles (magnetic field), split conducting rings R1/R2, carbon brushes B1/B2, axle and battery in the circuit (page 3).

solution: An electric motor is used in many electrical appliances such as electric fans, mixers/grinders, washing machines, water pumps, refrigerators, coolers and hair dryers, where electrical energy is converted into mechanical (rotational) energy.

stem:
Identify saturated and unsaturated hydrocarbon from the given structural formula:
(1) \(\mathrm{H_3C\!-\!CH_3}\) (each carbon bonded to hydrogens by single bonds - ethane)
(2) \(\mathrm{H_2C\!=\!CH_2}\) (a carbon-carbon double bond - ethene)
solution:
(1) \(\mathrm{CH_3\!-\!CH_3}\) (ethane) has only single bonds between carbon atoms, so it is a saturated hydrocarbon.
(2) \(\mathrm{CH_2\!=\!CH_2}\) (ethene) has a carbon-carbon double bond, so it is an unsaturated hydrocarbon.

stem: Draw electron dot structure for (1) ethane \(\mathrm{C_2H_6}\) and (2) ethene \(\mathrm{C_2H_4}\).
solution:
(1) Ethane \(\mathrm{C_2H_6}\): The two carbon atoms are joined by a single covalent bond (one shared electron pair), and each carbon shares one electron pair with three hydrogen atoms. Thus each carbon has four shared pairs (single C-C bond and three C-H bonds), giving \(\mathrm{H_3C\!:\!CH_3}\) with each bond as one shared electron pair.
(2) Ethene \(\mathrm{C_2H_4}\): The two carbon atoms are joined by a double covalent bond (two shared electron pairs, C::C), and each carbon shares one electron pair with two hydrogen atoms, giving \(\mathrm{H_2C\!::\!CH_2}\). In both, all atoms complete their octet/duplet through the shared electron pairs.

stem: Define Homologous series.
solution: A homologous series is a series of organic compounds having the same general formula and similar chemical properties, in which each successive member differs from the previous one by a \(\mathrm{-CH_2-}\) group (i.e. by a mass of 14 u). The members show a gradual change in physical properties with increasing molecular mass.
